units.source_text: 帅皇子答道：“不论何种技艺，若不专心研习，总无成就之望。

en.t: The Handsome Prince replied, "No matter what art or skill it may be, if one does not study it with devotion, there can be no hope of achievement.

units.source_text: 但各种技艺，均有师匠，均有法则。

en.t: But every art has its teachers, and every art has its rules.

units.source_text: 若能从师如法研习，深浅姑置不论，总可模拟师匠，多少有所成就。

en.t: If one studies under a teacher according to the proper method, then whether the learning is deep or shallow, one can at least imitate the master and achieve something.

units.source_text: 惟有书画之道与下围棋之事，甚是奇特，全凭天才做主。

en.t: Only the arts of calligraphy and painting, and the playing of go, are truly peculiar; in them everything depends on natural genius.

units.source_text: 常见庸碌之人，并不深刻钻研，只是富有天才，便能擅长书画，精通棋道。

en.t: One often sees ordinary people who have not studied deeply, yet because they are gifted, they excel at calligraphy and painting and master the way of go.

units.source_text: 富贵子弟之中，亦有超类拔群之人，百般技艺皆能通晓。

en.t: Among the children of noble and wealthy families, too, there are outstanding people who understand all manner of arts.

units.source_text: 父皇膝下我等皇子、皇女，无不研习各种技艺。

en.t: We princes and princesses raised at our father's side all studied many different arts.

units.source_text: 惟吾兄最为父皇所重视，又最善于承受教益。

en.t: But my elder brother was valued most highly by our father, and he was also the best at absorbing instruction.

units.source_text: 因而文才之丰富，自不必说。

en.t: Therefore, it goes without saying that his literary talent was abundant.

units.source_text: 其他诸艺之中，弹琴首屈一指，其次横笛、琵琶、筝，无不擅长。

en.t: Among the other arts, his playing of the koto ranked first; next came the transverse flute, the biwa, and the zither, all of which he played skillfully.
Our father himself once judged him in just this way.
People in the world all shared the same opinion.

units.source_text: 至于绘画，大家以为非吾兄所专精，仅乃偶尔兴到之时弄笔戏墨而已。

en.t: As for painting, everyone thought it was not my brother's specialty, but merely something he played at with brush and ink when the mood struck him.

units.source_text: 又谁知如此高明，直教古代名家退避三舍，竟令人不敢置信，反而觉得岂有此理了！”

en.t: Who could have known he was so brilliant that he would make even the famous masters of old step aside? It is so hard to believe that it almost seems unreasonable!"

units.source_text: 说到这里，已经语无伦次。

en.t: By the time he had said this much, his words had already become incoherent.

units.source_text: 大约是酒后好哭吧，所以说起桐壶院的往事，他便流着泪，颓丧不堪了。

en.t: Perhaps drink had made him tearful, for when he began speaking of the late Kiritsubo Emperor, he shed tears and became utterly dejected.
